criteria.requirement: Arming window defaults to 2000 ms with a hard maximum of 10000 ms and a minimum of 250 ms; any out-of-range, non-integer or non-numeric value is a configuration error refused before browser launch; one lease authorises exactly one protected-action attempt, is never refreshed or extended, and expiry fails closed; the first matching protected request consumes the lease and redirect continuation is part of that consumed attempt, minting and refreshing nothing: every hop is evaluated against the method actually observed on that hop and never inferred from the status code, a hop preserving a non-GET method must stay on the approved normalised origin, path and method (307/308 included), a hop observed to become GET is evaluated under ordinary GET route and origin policy and is never assumed side-effect-free, and expiry, ambiguity, an unobservable method, cross-origin movement, an unexpected path change or a method mismatch aborts the chain; every hop stays under the redirect cap and the chain under windowMs + 5000 ms with an absolute maximum of 30000 ms; at most one transmission of the approved non-GET body occurs per approval, enforced by a lease transmission counter and audited per transmission, so a same-target 307/308 continuation is aborted once a transmission has occurred (redirect_would_retransmit_approved_body); the chain deadline is min(windowMs + 5000, 30000) ms, computed by a pure bounded function chainDeadlineMs(windowMs, graceMs, absoluteMaxMs) that is unit-tested with synthetic inputs outside the configurable range (0, 250, 2000, 10000, 10001, 24999, 25000, 25001 and 1e9), so the 30000 ms cap is tested at the only place it is reachable while runtime configuration still refuses any windowMs outside 250..10000, non-integer or non-numeric before browser launch and never clamps; and the SPIKE-R outcome is applied per hop class: an enforceable class ships the method-observed rules with the transmission counter, an observable-only class permits a hop only when the observed method, origin and canonical path equal the approved triple and no transmission has yet occurred and otherwise aborts, and an unobservable class alone is refused before arming (POLICY_REDIRECT_UNOBSERVABLE, exit 18); Falcon never emulates a chain the browser did not expose, and a protected non-GET that is not redirected is unaffected

criteria.requirement: Evaluated from the shipped test harness with every repository file unmodified and using only the public surface, the fixture approval authority cannot be made to target any non-loopback origin, cannot be pointed at any server object other than the one this authority received from PilotFixtureServer.start() in this process, compared by reference identity in a module-private registry and never by shape, with the recorded listen epoch, port and family equal to the live values, so a prototype-built fake on net.Server.prototype, an independently created real loopback server including a forwarding one, a server from another authority or another run, a server transferred from another process, and a closed or closed-and-reopened server are all refused, cannot yield its per-run capability, and cannot cause any write under run/, data/ or the repository: the filesystem is byte-identical after the attempt suite. The attempt surface is bounded and exhaustive: argument values; own-property assignment, deletion and defineProperty on every returned object; pollution of Object.prototype, Array.prototype and Function.prototype for the keys the design reads (scope, binding, server, listening, address, family, port, manifestDigest; capabilityProof is never read off the approval, which is null-prototype so prototype pollution is not even inherited-visible on it); duck-typed substitutes for the server, approval, source and resolver; wrapper and shadowing sources; serialisation, structured clone and cross-process replay; the proxy and forwarding paths; and literal require of every production module under src/core/pilot/ with adversarial arguments, including a call to the ledger writer, which must refuse. Out of scope as repository modification accepted under OWNER-10: monkeypatching intrinsics, require.cache, Module._load, createRequire or any non-literal require, process.binding, child_process, worker_threads or a pty from a new or edited test file, and any edit to a repository file. The authority's transitive literal require graph contains no fs, fs/promises, SafeFs, ApprovalStore, AuditLog, RunToken or child_process module, no src/ or scripts/ file requires any tests/ path, and the require-graph walker resolves require(path.join(<literals>)) and fails closed on any other non-literal require. Any demonstrated path to an arbitrary target or to persisted approval state within that bounded surface is a blocker that stops 18D.Every in-scope case is a named automated runtime test with its named inversion, enumerated in rev 12 sections 6h.1 and 6h.2: the M-16 forge set (prototype constructor, Reflect.construct with an attacker newTarget, class extends), copy, spread, structuredClone, JSON round trip, Object.create, prototype replacement, plain and revoked Proxy, predicate non-transfer, prototype pollution before and after module load, deep-frozen writes on every nested path asserted as value-unchanged rather than as a throw because a frozen write is a silent no-op in sloppy CommonJS, rejection of Date, Buffer and typed-array fields at seal, the eight binding-field substitutions, reuse of one consumed approval against a different plan, manifest, role, origin, action and build as six separate sub-cases, PilotRuntime option injection and non-singleton source, the PilotRuntime-built-gate refusal of an unbranded approval, the in-process writer refusal under both piped stdio and a pty, the runtime mint scan that calls every exported function under src/core/pilot/ with adversarial arguments and asserts no reachable object satisfies the predicate, the duck-typed, prototype-built, independently created, foreign-run, cross-process, closed and closed-and-reopened server cases, the 0.0.0.0 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 binds, the full address-alias list, capability serialisation by JSON, structuredClone, v8.serialize and child-process transfer, a duck-typed authority and resolver, and the byte-identical filesystem assertion. A static assertion is additive defence in depth and never satisfies a case that can be run at runtime.

criteria.requirement: No production code distinguishes a ledger approval from any other object by a scope string, a constructor, a prototype, an instanceof test or any value readable off the object: there is no class brand and no reachable constructor anywhere in the discriminator path. The sole discriminator is membership in a module-private WeakSet held in ApprovalStore's closure, whose add and has are captured from WeakSet.prototype at module load and whose registering function is never exported, and registration happens only inside ApprovalStore's private verified-consumption path after chain, binding, build-identity, run-token, lock and exclusive-marker verification; the module exports the membership predicate only, and no brand, register, add, seal, mint, symbol, registry or writer surface exists anywhere in the module graph. Every approval is built with Object.create(null), carries no scope field, holds primitives only (no Date, Buffer, typed array, Map, Set or function — timestamps are epoch-millisecond integers), and is deep-frozen with every nested object also null-prototype and frozen; a failure of the frozen, null-prototype or field-type assertion is PILOT_INTERNAL_ERROR exit 18, approval_not_sealed. ApprovalStore exposes no writer; the interactive ledger writer is an entry-only module whose exports expose no callable writer when it is not the process entry (exit 1, approve_writer_not_entry), reached only by falcon.js --approve-action after falcon.js asserts it is itself the process entry (else exit 1, falcon_not_entry), and which refuses unless CI and GITHUB_ACTIONS are unset, tty.isatty(0) and tty.isatty(1) hold by syscall, a prompt bound to the plan digest, role, origin, method, canonical path, manifest digest, build id and approvals root real path is rendered before the challenge is generated, and that freshly generated random challenge is typed back on fd 0 with no parameter, option, environment key, config key or file by which it can be supplied; every prompt rendered, including each refusal, is appended to the audit chain. Any unbranded approval is fixture-class whatever it declares; in a PilotRuntime-built gate it is refused outright (APPROVAL_REQUIRED exit 14, fixture_approval_in_production_runtime), and in a directly constructed gate it is consumable only against a live loopback-literal origin and port read through net.Server intrinsics captured at module load (instanceof net.Server, net.Server.prototype.address and the prototype listening getter, whose absence fails closed exit 18) with a timing-safe capability proof held in a gate-side WeakMap keyed by the approval object and never present on the object; otherwise APPROVAL_REQUIRED exit 14. Captured net intrinsics authenticate nothing: they prevent own-property substitution only.
criteria.components: ApprovalStore closure-held ledger WeakSet with captured add/has and no exported registration surface + Object.create(null) approvals with primitives-only fields and total deep freeze + gate-side capability WeakMap + approve-action.js entry-only interactive writer with bound prompt and audited prompts + falcon.js entry assertion and spawnSync re-execution + PilotActionGate.perform ordered checks + PilotRuntime reference-identity source check, closed option allowlist and unbranded-approval refusal + PilotFixtureServer reference-identity server registry with listen epoch (rev 12 sections 6a-6d, 6g; closes SEC-11 M-16 and m-34, m-35, m-36)

criteria.requirement: The production interactive approval path is exercised by one automated test of the human interface, which creates no second approval mechanism and adds no code to src/: it spawns node falcon.js --approve-action under a pty against a hermetic loopback fixture, with fresh approvals and audit roots under os.tmpdir() passed as command arguments and never through an environment variable or flag, an environment stripped to an explicit allowlist with no key matching *_KEY, *_TOKEN, *_SECRET, *_PASSWORD, CI, GITHUB_*, proxy variables or NODE_OPTIONS and with HOME replaced, and a network gate asserting zero non-loopback requests. It parses the real prompt and asserts all eight bound values — plan digest, role, origin, HTTP method, canonical path, manifest digest, falconBuild id and approvals root real path — types the generated challenge exactly once through the pty, asserts exit 0 and exactly one verifying ledger entry, then asserts that replay yields APPROVAL_REQUIRED exit 14 and that each of the eight single-field binding substitutions yields exit 14, removes all approval state in teardown, and asserts the real run/ and data/ digest sets are byte-identical. A source scan asserts that no CLI flag, environment key, config key or file supplies the challenge or bypasses the interaction, consistent with OWNER-09. The test is local and manual only, because AC-084 fails on any approve flag reachable from a workflow; CI runs only the deterministic negative half — piped stdio, CI set, a wrong challenge and the in-process require refusal — and the AC-084 walker. Documentation states that it proves the production interaction path and does not authorise CI to approve real customer actions. Each assertion has a named inversion: removing the isatty gate, accepting a challenge from argv or environment, generating the challenge before rendering the prompt, omitting any bound prompt line, dropping the consumption marker, relaxing one binding field or dropping the environment allowlist must each make the test fail.
